堆叠商店功能默认禁用。 你可以在 config.yml 中配置启用它。 shop: # 允许 QuickShop 交易出售一捆多个物品吗？ allow-stacks: true # 允许创建堆叠商店时是否展示堆叠物品的效果。 # 对虚拟展示物品无效。 display-allow-stacks: true 另外，创建堆叠商店需要额外的权限，包含在 quickshop.player 中，可以在 Permissions 中详细浏览。
只需手持多个物品，按普通商店创建教程那样创建即可，如下图所示： 输入价格后即可。 注意：一捆的物品数量不可超过原版的物品最大堆叠数。
若需要修改堆叠商店里出售一捆的物品数量，只需输入命令 /quickshop size <newamount> 即可。
这个功能会给玩家推荐物品定价，输入命令 /quickshop suggestprice 即可。 某个物品生成推荐价格需要服务器上至少存在三个满足如下条件的商店： 不能是需要推荐价格的商店本身 交易的物品必须相同 交易类型必须相同（出售、收购等） 必须使用同一种货币（多经济模式下）

QuickShop-Hikari 6.3 introduces a player-specific Shop Tag System for organizing and tracking shops. Tags allow each player to create their own view of the server's shops. A tag belongs to the player who applied it, so tagging a shop does not modify the shop for everyone else. The system also powers QuickShop's built-in: Favorites Watch list Avoid list

Tags are stored using three pieces of information: Player → Shop → Tag For example, two players can tag the same shop differently: Player A → Shop 125 → #diamonds Player A → Shop 125 → #cheap Player B → Shop 125 → #restock Player A's tags do not appear in Player B's tag collection. This makes tags useful for personal shop organization without requiring shop owners or administrators to define global categories.

Custom tags can be applied with: /qs tag <tag> or explicitly: /qs tag add <tag> By default, QuickShop applies the tag to the shop the player is looking at. For example: /qs tag diamonds QuickShop displays custom tags with a # prefix: #diamonds You may also enter a custom tag with the hash: /qs tag #diamonds QuickShop normalizes the tag before storing it.

Before storing a tag, QuickShop normalizes it. Normalization includes: trimming whitespace; converting the tag to lowercase; removing a leading #; validating allowed characters; enforcing the maximum tag length; preventing custom commands from using reserved system tags. For example: #Diamonds is stored as: diamonds and displayed as: #diamonds

Remove a specific tag from a shop with: /qs tag remove <tag> Aliases for remove include: del delete For example: /qs tag remove diamonds removes #diamonds from the selected shop for the player executing the command.
To remove all of your tags from a shop: /qs tag clear This only removes tags applied by the player executing the command. It does not remove tags that other players have applied to the same shop.
Use: /qs tag list to view your tags on a shop. The list is paginated: /qs tag list <page> Each displayed tag can be used to navigate the tag system and remove or inspect tags.
Use: /qs tag shops to see shops that you have tagged. You can specify a page: /qs tag shops <page> QuickShop displays the number of tags you have associated with each shop.

Use: /qs tag tagged <tag> to list shops that you have marked with a particular tag. For example: /qs tag tagged diamonds lists your shops tagged: #diamonds Pagination is supported: /qs tag tagged diamonds 2

If you no longer want to use a particular custom tag, remove it from all of your tagged shops with: /qs tag purge <tag> Aliases include: /qs tag removefromall <tag> /qs tag untagall <tag> For example: /qs tag purge diamonds removes your #diamonds tag wherever you have applied it.
documents.s: Removing a Tag From All Your Shops

documents.t: QuickShop also provides: /qs tag clearall This clears the tag database globally and therefore requires a separate administrative permission. danger /qs tag clearall is not the same as /qs tag clear. clear removes the current player's tags from one shop. clearall removes all stored shop tags.

QuickShop reserves several internal tags for built-in player features: @fav @watch @avoid These tags should not normally be managed through /qs tag. Instead, use their dedicated commands. System Tag Feature Command @fav Favorite shops /qs favorite @watch Watched shops /qs watch @avoid Avoided shops /qs avoid System tags use the same underlying tag infrastructure as custom tags.

To toggle a shop as a favorite: /qs favorite Running the command again on the same shop removes it from your favorites. To list favorite shops: /qs favorite list or: /qs favorite list <page> Internally, Favorites use the reserved: @fav system tag.
To toggle a shop on your watch list: /qs watch Run the command again to remove the shop. List watched shops with: /qs watch list or: /qs watch list <page> Internally, the Watch system uses: @watch
To toggle a shop on your avoid list: /qs avoid Run the command again to remove it. List avoided shops with: /qs avoid list or: /qs avoid list <page> Internally, the Avoid system uses: @avoid

Command Description /qs tag <tag> Add a custom tag to a shop /qs tag add <tag> Add a custom tag /qs tag remove <tag> Remove a tag from a shop /qs tag clear Remove your tags from a shop /qs tag list [page] List your tags on a shop /qs tag shops [page] List shops you have tagged /qs tag tagged <tag> [page] List shops matching one of your tags /qs tag purge <tag> Remove one tag from all of your shops /qs tag clearall Globally clear all tags /qs favorite Toggle a favorite shop /qs favorite list [page] List favorite shops /qs watch Toggle a watched shop /qs watch list [page] List watched shops /qs avoid Toggle an avoided shop /qs avoid list [page] List avoided shops
The tag commands use dedicated QuickShop permissions.

quickshop.tag quickshop.tag.add quickshop.tag.delete quickshop.tag.clear quickshop.tag.clearall quickshop.tag.list quickshop.tag.shops quickshop.tag.tagged quickshop.tag.purge The base: quickshop.tag permission is checked before the /qs tag command can be used. Individual operations then check their corresponding child permission.
quickshop.favorite quickshop.favorite.list
quickshop.watch quickshop.watch.list
quickshop.avoid quickshop.avoid.list

Tags are persisted in QuickShop's database. QuickShop also maintains an in-memory tag index for fast lookups. This allows operations such as: Which tags has this player applied to this shop? Which shops has this player tagged #diamonds? How many tags has this player applied? Does this player have @fav on this shop? without repeatedly scanning every shop.

Tags are associated with QuickShop's persistent shop IDs. QuickShop's tag-management API includes operations for clearing all tags belonging to a shop, allowing tag records to be cleaned up when the associated shop is removed.

The tag system is exposed through the QuickShop API. Get the active TagManager with: TagManager tags = QuickShopAPI.getInstance().getTagManager(); The manager supports operations including: addTag(...) toggleTag(...) removeTag(...) hasTag(...) tagsFilteredByShop(...) shopsFilteredByTag(...) shopsFilteredByTags(...) removeAllShopTags(...) removeAllShopTagsBy(...) removeAllPlayerTags(...) removeAllTags(...) totalTags() totalTagsByPlayer(...) tagsCount(...) Tags are player-specific, so most query and modification methods require the player's UUID.

QuickShopAPI api = QuickShopAPI.getInstance(); TagManager tags = api.getTagManager(); TaggingResult result = tags.addTag( shop.getShopId(), player.getUniqueId(), "diamonds" ); For custom input, normalize the tag first: String tag = tags.service().normalizeTag( input, false ); if(tag != null) { tags.addTag( shop.getShopId(), player.getUniqueId(), tag ); } The second argument to normalizeTag controls whether reserved system tags are allowed. For normal custom tags, use: false
documents.s: Adding a Tag Through the API

documents.t: Retrieve a player's tags for one shop: Set<String> shopTags = tags.tagsFilteredByShop( player.getUniqueId(), shop.getShopId() );

Find the shops a player tagged with a specific value: List<Long> shops = tags.shopsFilteredByTag( player.getUniqueId(), "diamonds" ); The returned values are persistent QuickShop shop IDs. Multiple tags can also be used as filter criteria: List<Long> shops = tags.shopsFilteredByTags( player.getUniqueId(), List.of("diamonds", "cheap") );
boolean favorite = tags.hasTag( shop.getShopId(), player.getUniqueId(), TagService.SYS_FAV );

The high-level manager provides: tags.toggleTag( shop.getShopId(), player.getUniqueId(), TagService.SYS_FAV ); QuickShop's Favorite, Watch, and Avoid commands use this behavior to toggle their reserved tags.

The underlying: TagService handles lower-level operations such as: tag normalization; tag display formatting; database persistence; command mapping; reserved system tags. It is available from: tags.service(); Most addons should use TagManager for normal tag operations and use TagService when normalization or lower-level persistence behavior is specifically required.

The Shop Tag System provides personal organization on top of QuickShop's persistent shops. Players can create custom categories such as: #diamonds #cheap #restock #spawn while QuickShop's built-in Favorite, Watch, and Avoid features use the same system through reserved tags. Because tags are stored per player and per shop, every player can organize the marketplace independently without changing the shop itself.
QuickShop 的税收系统可以让服主有更多维护经济平衡的选择。 这个系统在 6.2.0.11+ 进行了更新 新系统允许： 对店主收税 对买家收税 对双方收税 使用渐进式税收门槛 配置自定义税收行为 这个系统替代了旧版本的税收配置。
在商店交易中： 计算商店价格。 基于配置计算税收。 从对应目标收取税。 剩余资金正常分配。 你可以配置： 固定百分比税 基于玩家余额的渐进式税 税收账户 流动规则
新系统允许你根据经济门槛征收税费。 示例： 0 – 10000 余额 → 1% 的税收 10000 – 100000 → 2% 的税收 100000+ → 3% 的税收 这可以防止极端富有的玩家破坏经济平衡。
你可以配置对谁收税： 店主 买家 双方 这可以让你根据服务器的经济玩法设计自由决定。

所有税收相关设置都位于 config.yml 下的 shop-tax 部分。 目前配置同时支持固定税与渐进式税收： shop-tax: # 选择使用的税收类型： # basic = 固定税率 # progressive = 基于玩家资产收税 type: basic # 收取税费的账户名称。 # 设置为空表示禁用存入（仍会收税）。 account: tax # 在交易信息中显示收取税费。 show: false # 不收取无限商店的税费。 disable-for-unlimited-shop: false # 对谁收税，店主或参与交互的玩家。 # player - 与商店交互的玩家。 # shop - 对店主。 # payee - 对收款方。 # both - 对玩家和店主。 apply-to: player basic: # 固定税率（小数格式） # 示例：0.05 = 5% rate: 0.05 progressive: brackets: '10000': 0.01 '50000': 0.02 '250000': 0.03 '1000000': 0.05 '5000000': 0.08 '-1': 0.12 请在更新到 6.2.0.11 之后详细检查配置，因为旧税收系统已经更新。
税收功能可以： 适当销毁流通货币 支持服务器银行或城镇 创建销毁机制 缓解通货膨胀 奖励活跃玩家
新税收制度： 灵活 可配置 注重平衡 为现代经济服务器设计 确保在升级后详细检查配置。

QuickShop-Hikari 6.3 adds Text Displays, allowing shop information to be shown as floating text above a shop's displayed item. Text Displays use Minecraft's native TextDisplay entities and support Adventure/MiniMessage formatting, allowing server owners to create more informative and visually customized shop displays. warning Text Displays currently only work with the Display Entity display system: shop: display-type: 3 They do not currently work with display-type: 2. See Shop Display System for information about configuring shop item displays.

Text Displays are disabled by default. Enable them in config.yml: shop: display-type: 3 text-display: enabled: true When enabled, QuickShop creates a separate floating text entity alongside the shop's item display. note Enabling text-display.enabled does not change the configured item display type. shop.display-type must still be set to 3.

A Text Display configuration looks similar to: shop: display-type: 3 text-display: enabled: true range-blocks: 3 y-offset: 0.8 background-color: 1073741824 line-width: 200 text-opacity: -1 see-through: false shadow: enabled: true scale: x: 0.5 y: 0.5 z: 0.5 lines: - "<green><item_name></green>" - "<gray><owner></gray>" - "<gray><type></gray>" - "<gold><price_amount></gold>" The lines section controls the information shown to players, while the other settings control the appearance and visibility of the display.

The contents of a Text Display are configured through: shop: text-display: lines: - "<green><item_name></green>" - "<gray><owner></gray>" - "<gray><type></gray>" - "<gold><price_amount></gold>" Each entry creates a new line in the floating display. The lines use QuickShop's RenderComponent system. This allows shop information to be inserted into the text while still allowing normal text and MiniMessage formatting around it. For example: lines: - "<gold>Item:</gold> <item_name>" - "<yellow>Owner:</yellow> <owner>" - "<yellow>Price:</yellow> <price_amount>"

Text Displays support Adventure/MiniMessage formatting. For example: lines: - "<bold><gold><item_name></gold></bold>" - "<gray>Sold by <white><owner></white></gray>" - "<green><price_amount></green>" This can be used to customize colors, decorations, and other supported MiniMessage formatting. tip RenderComponents such as <item_name> and <owner> can be combined with MiniMessage tags and normal text on the same line.
RenderComponents insert information from the shop into a configured line.
Displays the shop item's name. - "<green><item_name></green>" Example output: Diamond
Displays the amount of the item being traded. - "<gray>Amount: <amount></gray>"
Displays applicable level information for the shop item, such as an enchantment level or potion duration. - "<gray><item_level></gray>"
Displays the shop owner's name. - "<gray>Owner: <owner></gray>"

Displays the formatted shop price without the additional amount formatting used by price_amount. - "<gold><price_solo></gold>" note Earlier 6.3 development versions used price for this component. It was renamed to price_solo.
Displays the formatted shop price with the applicable trade amount. - "<gold><price_amount></gold>" This is generally the most useful price component for the default Text Display layout.
Displays the shop's current stock information. - "<gray>Stock: <stock></gray>"
Displays the shop type. - "<gray><type></gray>" For example, this can represent whether the shop is buying or selling.
Displays the shop's current state or status. - "<gray>Status: <status></gray>"

amount_auto is a conditional RenderComponent that changes its output depending on the shop's current state. - "<gray>Stock: <amount_auto></gray>" It can represent: the remaining stock amount when stock is available; an out-of-stock state when the shop has no remaining stock; an unlimited state when the shop has unlimited stock. This makes it useful when you want one line to automatically represent several possible stock conditions.
lines: - "<green><item_name></green>" - "<gold><price_amount></gold>" This provides a compact display showing only the item and price.

lines: - "<bold><green><item_name></green></bold>" - "<gray>Owner: <white><owner></white></gray>" - "<gray>Type: <white><type></white></gray>" - "<gold><price_amount></gold>" This provides more information without displaying stock.
lines: - "<bold><green><item_name></green></bold>" - "<gold><price_amount></gold>" - "<gray>Stock: <amount_auto></gray>" The final line automatically changes based on the shop's stock state.

The maximum configured viewing range is controlled by: shop: text-display: range-blocks: 3 This controls how far away the Text Display can be rendered. Lower values can help keep floating shop information limited to players who are close to the shop, while larger values make the information visible from farther away.

The Text Display is positioned above the shop's item display. Its vertical offset is controlled by: shop: text-display: y-offset: 0.8 Increasing the value moves the text upward: y-offset: 1.2 Decreasing it moves the text closer to the displayed item: y-offset: 0.5 Decimal values are supported.

The size of the Text Display can be adjusted independently on each axis: shop: text-display: scale: x: 0.5 y: 0.5 z: 0.5 Using the same value for all three axes keeps the text proportionally scaled. For example, a larger display could use: scale: x: 0.75 y: 0.75 z: 0.75 Changing the axes independently can distort the text and is generally unnecessary for normal shop layouts.

The Text Display background is controlled by: shop: text-display: background-color: 1073741824 The value is a 32-bit ARGB color value. The default value is: 1073741824 which uses Minecraft's default Text Display background behavior. Changing this value allows the background behind the floating text to be customized.

Text opacity is controlled with: shop: text-display: text-opacity: -1 -1 uses full opacity. The supported opacity values are 0 through 255, although very low values may be treated as effectively invisible by Minecraft's rendering system. For normal readable displays, leaving this at the default value is recommended unless a transparent or faded appearance is specifically desired.

A shadow can be rendered behind the text: shop: text-display: shadow: enabled: true Disable it with: shadow: enabled: false Text shadows can improve readability when the display is viewed against bright or visually complex blocks.

Text Displays can optionally remain visible through blocks: shop: text-display: see-through: false Enable this behavior with: see-through: true warning Enabling see-through can make shop information visible through walls and other solid blocks. Consider the layout of your server's shops before enabling it globally.

The display's line width is configured with: shop: text-display: line-width: 200 This controls the width used when rendering Text Display content. A smaller value causes long content to wrap sooner, while a larger value allows more text to fit before wrapping. For example: line-width: 120 can create a narrower display, while: line-width: 300 provides more horizontal space.

The following configuration creates a compact Text Display with the item name, shop owner, price, and current stock state: shop: display-type: 3 text-display: enabled: true range-blocks: 3 y-offset: 0.8 background-color: 1073741824 line-width: 200 text-opacity: -1 see-through: false shadow: enabled: true scale: x: 0.5 y: 0.5 z: 0.5 lines: - "<bold><green><item_name></green></bold>" - "<gray>Owner: <white><owner></white></gray>" - "<gold><price_amount></gold>" - "<gray>Stock: <amount_auto></gray>" This configuration requires: shop: display-type: 3 because Text Displays currently only work with QuickShop's Display Entity display system.

The Shop Trade Menu is QuickShop-Hikari's player-facing GUI for buying from and selling to shops. Instead of requiring repeated direct interactions with the shop, the menu provides a configurable inventory interface with: the shop item; current stock or available space; formatted price information; the shop owner; preset quantity buttons; custom amount entry; a configurable close button. The Trade Menu is configured through gui.yml.

The GUI is opened by QuickShop's Interaction Manager through the: TRADE_UI interaction behavior. When TRADE_UI handles an existing shop, QuickShop first checks that the shop is not frozen. Frozen shops cannot be traded with through the menu. Before opening the GUI, QuickShop asynchronously calculates the shop's remaining stock: shop.shopType().remainingStockAsync(shop) The calculated value is stored with the menu viewer and used when rendering the Trade Menu. note The menu's stock information is therefore prepared asynchronously before the GUI opens instead of requiring a synchronous stock calculation during menu rendering.

The Trade Menu is configured under: trade: in gui.yml. The default menu uses six inventory rows: trade: title: "lang:gui.trade.title" rows: 6 The default layout includes: Element Default Slot Shop item 13 Stock information 21 Price information 22 Seller information 23 Quantity buttons 37–42 Custom amount 43 Close button 49 The top, separator, and bottom rows use the configured border: border: material: GRAY_STAINED_GLASS_PANE name: " " rows: [1, 4, 6] All of these materials, slots, names, and lore can be changed in gui.yml.

The shop's actual item is displayed in the configured shop-item slot: shop-item: slot: 13 QuickShop fires its item-preview population event before placing the item in the menu, allowing compatible integrations to modify the displayed preview.

The stock icon defaults to: info-stock: material: CHEST name: "lang:gui.trade.info-stock.display" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.info-stock.lore" slot: 21 The value shown depends on the shop. QuickShop handles: normal stock counts; unlimited shops; out-of-stock states; shop states that override the normal shop-type text. The stock value is based on the remaining-stock result calculated before the Trade Menu is opened.

The default price icon is: info-price: material: GOLD_INGOT name: "lang:gui.trade.info-price.display" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.info-price.lore" slot: 22 QuickShop formats the price through the shop's active currency and economy formatting. For stacking shops, the menu also uses the shop item's configured stack amount when displaying quantity information.

The default seller icon is: info-seller: material: PLAYER_HEAD name: "lang:gui.trade.info-seller.display" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.info-seller.lore" slot: 23 For shops owned by real players, QuickShop applies the owner's UUID to the player-head profile. The displayed owner name comes from the shop owner's QuickShop user information.

Preset trade quantities are configured under: trade: quantity-buttons: The default configuration is: quantity-buttons: material-buy: LIME_CONCRETE material-sell: ORANGE_CONCRETE custom-model-data: 0 slots: [37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42] quantities: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64] close-after: true display-buy: "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.display-buy" display-sell: "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.display-sell" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.lore" Each entry in quantities corresponds to the entry in the same position in slots. For example: slots: [37, 38, 39] quantities: [1, 2, 4] creates three buttons trading one, two, or four shop units. important For a stacking shop, these values represent shop units, not necessarily individual items. If the shop sells stacks of 16 items, a quantity button configured as: quantities: [4] represents four shop units, or 64 actual items.

The visible amount used by each quantity button is calculated as: shop item amount × configured quantity For example, if the shop item amount is 8 and the button quantity is 4: 8 × 4 = 32 items The menu item stack itself is capped at Minecraft's normal visible stack size of 64, while the actual trade quantity still uses the configured shop-unit quantity.

QuickShop-Hikari 6.3 adds the close-after setting for quantity buttons. trade: quantity-buttons: close-after: true When: close-after: true the Trade Menu closes after the player clicks a preset quantity button. When: close-after: false QuickShop keeps the player on the Trade Menu page after the action, allowing repeated trades without reopening the GUI. The default is: close-after: true This setting applies to the preset quantity buttons.

Players can also enter an exact amount through the custom amount button: custom-amount: material: NAME_TAG name: "lang:gui.trade.custom-amount.display" slot: 43 Clicking the button opens QuickShop's chat-input flow. The entered value represents the actual number of items the player wants to trade. QuickShop then validates the amount against the shop's configured item amount. For example, if a stacking shop trades: 16 items per shop unit valid custom amounts include: 16 32 48 64 but: 20 is rejected because it is not divisible by the shop-unit amount. Internally, QuickShop normalizes the player-entered item quantity into shop units: normalized quantity = entered item amount / shop item amount This normalized quantity is then passed into QuickShop's trade logic.

For limited shops, QuickShop verifies that the normalized quantity does not exceed the available stock. If it does, the trade is rejected and the player receives the configured invalid-stock message. Unlimited shops are not subject to this stock check.

Entering: 0 does not perform a trade. Non-numeric input causes QuickShop to display the custom amount prompt again. Values that are not valid multiples of the shop's trade amount produce the configured: trade.invalid-multiple message.

The same Trade Menu is used for both shop directions. For a shop that sells items to players, the GUI uses the buy visual configuration: material-buy: LIME_CONCRETE display-buy: "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.display-buy" For a shop that buys items from players, it uses: material-sell: ORANGE_CONCRETE display-sell: "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.display-sell" QuickShop then delegates the transaction to its normal shop trading logic rather than implementing a separate GUI-specific economy transaction. This means Trade Menu transactions still use QuickShop's normal: economy handling; tax handling; inventory checks; stock checks; permissions; shop behavior.

Trade execution from the GUI is scheduled through QuickShop's region-thread helper: Util.regionThread(...) This allows the Trade Menu to work with QuickShop's modern server-threading support rather than assuming that all Bukkit operations should run from one global server thread.
The default close button is: close: material: BARRIER name: "lang:gui.shared.close.display" slot: 49 Clicking it closes the menu without performing a transaction.

Trade Menu names and lore can use QuickShop language entries by prefixing values with: lang: For example: name: "lang:gui.trade.info-price.display" or: lore: - "lang:gui.trade.info-price.lore" QuickShop resolves those values through its localization system. Direct MiniMessage-formatted strings can also be used: name: "<gold>Price</gold>"

gui.yml supports Adventure MiniMessage formatting for menu text. For example: name: "<bold><green>Buy Items</green></bold>" Common tags include: <bold> <italic> <red> <green> <yellow> <aqua> <gradient:...>

Trade Menu icons support custom-model-data. For example: info-price: material: GOLD_INGOT custom-model-data: 1001 This can be used with a resource pack to give QuickShop GUI icons custom textures or models.

trade: title: "lang:gui.trade.title" rows: 6 border: material: GRAY_STAINED_GLASS_PANE name: " " rows: [1, 4, 6] shop-item: slot: 13 info-stock: material: CHEST name: "lang:gui.trade.info-stock.display" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.info-stock.lore" slot: 21 info-price: material: GOLD_INGOT name: "lang:gui.trade.info-price.display" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.info-price.lore" slot: 22 info-seller: material: PLAYER_HEAD name: "lang:gui.trade.info-seller.display" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.info-seller.lore" slot: 23 quantity-buttons: material-buy: LIME_CONCRETE material-sell: ORANGE_CONCRETE slots: [37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42] quantities: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64] close-after: true display-buy: "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.display-buy" display-sell: "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.display-sell" lore: - "lang:gui.trade.quantity-button.lore" custom-amount: material: NAME_TAG name: "lang:gui.trade.custom-amount.display" slot: 43 close: material: BARRIER name: "lang:gui.shared.close.display" slot: 49

The Trade Menu provides a configurable GUI over QuickShop's normal trading system. QuickShop-Hikari 6.3's important Trade Menu behavior includes: asynchronous remaining-stock calculation before opening; configurable preset quantities; correct stacking-shop quantity normalization; custom exact-item amount entry; configurable close-after behavior; configurable materials, slots, names, lore, and custom model data; MiniMessage and lang: localization support; region-thread-aware trade execution. For most servers, the default GUI provides a complete trading interface while gui.yml allows the visual layout and quantity choices to be adapted to the server's economy.
QuickShop 内置了 WorldEdit 与 FastAsyncWorldEdit（FAWE）的保护与联动。 在 6.2.0.11 版本之后，它不再是单独的兼容模块——它现在内置于 QuickShop 中。 无需下载或安装任何其他兼容插件。
WorldEdit 和 FAWE 允许管理员和建筑师： 复制并粘贴区域 替换大块区域 大规模删除区域 回滚区域 重新生成地形 在没有保护的情况下，这些操作会： 产生幽灵商店 在数据库中留下废弃数据条目 复制商店 清理容器而不清除商店数据 导致世界和数据库产生不一致问题 QuickShop 现在可以自动检测并安全处理 WorldEdit 和 FAWE 的编辑操作。
当 WorldEdit 或 FAWE 修改方块时： 通过 WorldEdit 删除的商店将被从数据库中正确删除。 商店数据保持与世界变化同步。 防止产生幽灵商店。 批量块替换将不会留下损坏的商店条目。 这适用于： //set //replace //cut //paste //regen 选区删除 大面积容器移除 无需额外配置。
插件完全支持 FastAsyncWorldEdit（FAWE）。 因为 FAWE 编辑进程采用异步处理，QuickShop 负责： 区域线程安全处理 异步方块更新 批量编辑期间安全删除商店 无需手动启用任何功能。
如果你正在使用 WorldEdit 删除容器（箱子、桶等）： QuickShop 将自动： 检测方块移除 解除注册商店 清理数据库条目 防止产生幽灵商店 一般情况下，无需在使用 WorldEdit 后输入 /qs cleanghost 命令。
documents.s: 通过 WorldEdit 删除商店

documents.t: 如果您复制并粘贴包含商店的区域： 商店数据不会错误复制。 商店 ID 仍会保持一致。 无效的粘贴商店不会自动注册，除非正确创建。 防止意外复制出现漏洞。
WorldEdit 和 FAWE 操作可以一次修改数千个方块。 QuickShop 会高效安全地处理这些： 批量清理 线程安全的选区访问（尤其对于 Folia 而言） 大规模编辑尽可能降低性能消耗
QuickShop 中没有特定的 WorldEdit 编辑配置。 如果检测到 WorldEdit 或 FAWE 则自动支持并始终启用。 若不安装 WorldEdit，则不会触发额外功能。
不需要。 在 6.2.0.11 之后，WorldEdit 支持已内置，无需独立的兼容模块。

QuickShop 内置了 WorldEdit 和 FAWE 兼容，可以： 保证大面积编辑安全 不会产生幽灵商店 自动清理数据库 安全处理线程 无需额外设置步骤 WorldEdit 支持现在是 QuickShop 的核心功能之一。
当您键入并执行快速shop命令时，您应该听到打字机的声音，可以在 config.yml 中进行更改。 这不是一个重要的功能，但可以有（为什么不呢 :)）。 无论如何，如果您不喜欢它们，可以禁用它们。
# 游戏内特殊效果 effect: # 声音相关 sound: # 玩家尝试使用 tab 补全时是否播放声音？ ontabcomplete: true # 玩家尝试执行命令时是否播放声音？ oncommand: true # 玩家点击商店容器/告示牌时是否播放声音？ onclick: true
QuickShop-Hikari 包括一个能够保持交易一致性和防止任何一方数据损坏的系统。 TL;DR 如果交易失败，QuickShop 将会回滚双方的钱和物品，将背包和金钱回滚到交易开始之前的状态。
目前，QuickShop-Hikari 支持两种类型的交易系统。
QuickShop 记录存款或提取的余额金额，并在交易失败时重新提取和重新存回。
QuickShop 将为商店容器的物品栏和玩家物品栏拍摄快照，并在交易失败时恢复快照。
这一页将会引导您在您的 Spigot 服务器上安装 QuickShop-Hikari。

Paper 系 Minecraft 服务端（高于 1.20 的版本，使用 Java 21） 用于桥接经济插件与 QuickShop 的 Vault。 显示虚拟展示物品和分玩家语言还需安装支持的发包库插件： ProtocolLib PacketEvents 任意兼容 Vault 的经济插件，例如 XConomy。 同样支持 EssentialsX。 一个权限管理插件，例如 LuckPerms. 本教程假设你使用的 QuickShop-Hikari、ProtocolLib、XConomy、Vault 以及 LuckPerms 插件都是最新版本，且系统环境为 Windows 11。 不过安装过程在 Linux 上也大致相似。
在安装 QuickShop-Hikari 之前，请确保您已经安装了所有前置插件：Vault、ProtocolLib 或 PacketEvents、XConomy（也可以是 EssentialsX）和 LuckPerms！ 下载插件，将其放入 plugins 文件夹。
如果同时安装了 ProtocolLib 与 PacketEvents，且你需要使用后者展示物品，那么你需要在 config.yml 中设置 shop.display-protocol: 'packetevents'。

从 Modrinth 下载最新版本的 QuickShop-Hikari。 请先忽略部分带有 Compat- 前缀的文件。 你需要获取的文件应当有一个 Primary 标签，如下图所示： 将 QuickShop 的 jar 文件放入 plugins 文件夹，启动服务器，然后在控制台输入 qs 命令。 如果插件安装正确，那么输入命令后会弹出帮助界面： 如果你碰到了报错，你可以浏览常见问题章节，或者加入我们的 Discord 聊天群组，在 #qsh-support 频道寻求帮助。
默认情况下，玩家无法创建商店。 要允许玩家创建和拥有商店，您必须授予他们必要的权限。 对大多数用户来说，你需要做的只是运行一个简单的命令： /lp group default permission set quickshop.player true 然后就大功告成了！ 玩家现在可以创建和使用商店，也可以使用其他功能。 对于进阶权限设置，请看这一章节。
documents.s: 配置 QuickShop 以允许玩家使用

documents.t: 现在，QuickShop-Hikari 正在您的服务器上运行。关于更多设置，请查看左侧的导航面板并阅读不同的部分。
documents.s: 一切就绪！ 可以开始使用了！

documents.t: 权限决定着 QuickShop 的大多数功能，你也可以用它们控制 QuickShop-Hikari 的相关功能。

要将一个权限节点授予一个权限组，您可以使用： 授予：/lp group <group> permission set <permission> true 要移除这个权限节点，请使用： 移除：/lp group <group> permission unset <permission> 若权限已包含在 简单权限 中，你可以通过禁用它将其覆写： 强制禁用：/lp group <group> permission set <permission> false 如果你不知道权限组的名字，请输入“default”。 了解 LuckPerms 相关的信息，可在这里阅读相关维基。
documents.s: 最简单的 LuckPerms 指南

documents.t: QuickShop 提供了一套简单的权限模板，方便您快速分配权限，它们是： quickshop.player，包含所有玩家需要的子权限节点。 quickshop.moderator，包含所有玩家需要的子权限节点。 使用简单权限的一大优势就是新版本引入的权限可以自动生效，无需额外配置。
这里是 QuickShop-Hikari 所有权限节点的详细列表。您可以使用命令授予 / 移除它们。 见 plugin.yml -> 权限节点。
